When it comes to assessing and analyzing antisemitism, it's of course important to have a consistent standard for doing so. Our organization has generally applied slide the IHRA definition of antisemitism, one of so much importance on this very day, which is International Holocaust Remembrance Day. The IHRA definition of antisemitism was established by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance in 2016, and it ultimately helps elucidate how antisemitism manifests both classically and contemporarily. One very important detail within the IHRA definition is it is important to analyze antisemitism within general context. The definition is not conclusive in any manner, but it definitely can be used as a sufficient guiding tool to understanding when and how antisemitism manifests in the current iterations. Unfortunately, over the last few millennia, antisemitism has managed to adjust and evolve to incorporate contemporary themes to make it palatable, and unfortunately many people continue to miss out on how modern antisemitism manifests. So we don't, of course, have a council or some sort of judicial committee to assess every incident of antisemitism and to declare whether or not it is antisemitism, but we do have objective guiding frameworks to help us understand how and when it manifests and to respond accordingly.
